description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of entity types identified within a biomedical text corpus. The chart contains 16 slices, each representing a different entity category. The largest slice, labeled “Chemical” and colored blue, occupies approximately 37% of the chart. “Protein” is the next largest, colored red and representing roughly 23% of the chart. Following this are “DNA” at 6%, “Chemical Family” at 5%, and “Disease” at 4%. The remaining slices, representing “Cell Type”, “Drug”, “Frequency”, “Cell Line”, “Strength”, “Form”, “Gene Or Gene Product”, “Disease Or Phenotypic Feature”, “Route”, “Sequence Entity”, “Molecular Function”, “Biological Process”, and “Reason”, each contribute a smaller proportion, ranging from approximately 1% to 3%. A legend is present on the right side of the chart, labeling each slice with its corresponding entity type. Percentage labels are not displayed directly on the slices, but are included in the legend. The slices appear to be ordered visually, with the largest slices positioned first and decreasing in size as they proceed around the circle.
